title: Noise Diffusion for Enhancing Semantic Faithfulness in Text-to-Image Synthesis
role: A vision-language score on the finished image that picks how the starting noise is replaced; its own control shows direct gradient updates barely change structure.
reads: The finished decoded image plus a yes-or-no question; the score is the probability of Yes, and no noisy input is read.
score_enters: An approximate gradient at the final latent chooses 1 of 50 random noises, which is mixed into the starting noise with step size 1 minus the square root of the score; best of the rounds is returned.
properties: Prompt match is measured by VQA and CLIP scores; attribute binding and spatial relation appear only in example images and through the overall VQA score; counting, position and size are not tested.
unseen: no: no held-out concepts are tested.
headline: VQA score (0 to 1, higher better, the optimised quantity) after 50 rounds on SD1.4 is 0.9790 on simple prompts, 0.1073 above InitNo, and 0.9578 on complex prompts, 0.1930 above InitNo.
copy_or_avoid: Copy the random-noise control; avoid reading the layout change as gradient steering, because noise replacement plus best-of-N selection can produce it (inferred).

extra_papers.why: Updates the latent at each denoising step from cross-attention between words and image.

disagreements.claim: The updated starting noise stays standard Gaussian for any step size.
disagreements.paper_says: The claim assumes Gaussian noise, but Algorithm 1 picks that noise by an argmax that depends on the current latent, so it is not independent of the latent (inferred).

disagreements.claim: The VLM score's gradient drives the change in the picture.
disagreements.paper_says: Methods following the gradient directly show limited structural change; the large changes come with noise replacement, including the random controls in Fig. 6.
